notes.1: A number of weaker candidates thought that mass could be determined by lowering an irregular object into a measuring cylinder half-full of water.
notes.2: Most candidates thought that the heavier stone would reach the floor first.
notes.3: Only stronger candidates answered this question well, with other responses evenly spread over the options. Candidates had to translate minutes into hours and to recognise that average speed is total distance divided by total time.
notes.4: Only stronger candidates had a secure understanding of the conservation of mass. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0625 Physics June 2021
notes.6: Weaker candidates did not subtract the mass of the empty flask in order to find the mass of the liquid.
notes.10: While stronger candidates answered correctly, a large number of other candidates believed that shining a light onto a block of iron does not transfer energy. For that to be true, the block would have to be reflecting the light perfectly, which is impossible.
notes.11: Weaker candidates did not realise that for the box to gain energy, work must be done on it, and that for work to be done, movement in the direction of the applied force is needed.
notes.12: To answer this question, candidates needed to know the formula for pressure and to be careful about unit conversions.
notes.13: The most popular option was C , indicating that many candidates did not know that there is a vacuum above the mercury.
notes.17: Only stronger candidates identified mass as the non-thermometric property. Other candidates were unable to demonstrate a secure knowledge of this area.
notes.18: Many candidates were able to spot the connection between a greater thermal capacity and a greater quantity of energy being needed, but then some confused thermal capacity with latent heat.
notes.19: Many candidates correctly identified that a longer strip of wax would melt but only the strongest of these were able to extend that idea to the earlier dropping of the pin.
notes.21: Only stronger candidates identified this wave as longitudinal.
notes.22: This question was usually answered well. The most common error was to confuse refraction and diffraction.
notes.23: Many candidates found this question challenging. At angles infinitesimally larger than θ , no light will emerge, so this is indeed the critical angle. And since the question declares that there is some light not travelling along the reflection path, it cannot be total internal reflection.
notes.26: While stronger candidates answered correctly, many weaker candidates chose option B .
notes.27: As many candidates selected option A as the correct option, B . Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0625 Physics June 2021
notes.29: The most popular response was A , possibly because candidates did not read the question carefully enough and were expecting negatively charged rods.
notes.30: While some candidates successfully added the two resistances, many then divided the total resistance by the potential difference rather than the other way round.
notes.33: This question proved challenging for many candidates and only the strongest had a secure concept of the role of a fuse to protect the cables between it and the appliance from overheating.
notes.36: A significant number of weaker candidates thought that one or other of the suggestions would have no effect.
notes.40: A significant number of weaker candidates thought that the half-life was half of the maximum time shown on the horizontal axis. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0625 Physics June 2021
